name: Arsenic

discovery.discoverer: Known since antiquity; first isolated by Albertus Magnus, c. 1250

occurrence: Found combined in sulfide ores (arsenopyrite); also contaminates some groundwater supplies naturally.
majorUses: Historically used as a poison and, ironically, as a medicine
safetyNotes: Notoriously toxic — arsenic poisoning was a historically favoured (and hard-to-detect) method of murder before the Marsh test made it identifiable in the 1830s.
notableCharacteristics: Sublimes directly from solid to gas rather than melting normally at standard pressure, which is why its 'boiling point' is actually listed lower than its melting behaviour under pressure.
whyHere: With five valence electrons like nitrogen and phosphorus above it, arsenic can form both +3 and +5 compounds, but its larger, more polarizable atom pushes it toward metalloid behaviour and notably toxic biochemistry.
didYouKnow: Arsenic poisoning went undetectable by any reliable chemical test until 1836, when the Marsh test was invented specifically to catch it — before that it was called 'inheritance powder' for how often it settled family disputes.
genZNote: The original untraceable poison until chemistry caught up. Also, somehow, in your phone's semiconductors now.
